subject: Hospitality
title: Convention Centers: Cities Within Cities
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Convention Centers: Cities Within Cities.

hook.text: The Las Vegas Convention Center spans 200,000 sqm—larger than 28 football fields.

buildup.text: Convention centers are massive public investments—$500M–$2B to build. Cities fund them because events fill hotels nearby.

discovery.text: The economic multiplier is powerful: a 10,000-person medical conference can generate $25+ million in local spending over four.

twist.text: Many convention centers lose money operationally. They survive because the indirect economic impact—hotel tax, restaurant revenue.

climax.text: Convention centers compete globally: Singapore, Dubai, Barcelona, and Chicago invest billions to attract major events.

punchline.text: Built to lose money, designed to make everyone else rich.

quiz.question: Why do cities invest in convention centers that often lose money operationally?
options: The indirect economic impact—hotel tax, restaurant, and retail revenue—justifies the investment
